business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Sultanate of Oman — onshore commercial registration at Muscat Governorate (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state incorporation distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — codified Sultani decree legislation (civil-law style) supplemented by Sharia-consistent residual principles and administrative regulations; unitary, non-federal legal system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Oman Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 January 2009 (investment chapter relevant to the Stripe Billing and ACH Direct payment rails of this PropTech SaaS entity)
India–Oman Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1997, as amended)
Netherlands–Oman Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree No. 18/2019 (Commercial Companies Law; governs SPC formation, shareholder register and beneficial-owner record-keeping), Royal Decree No. 30/2016 (Law on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism) with its consolidated Executive Regulations administered by the Omani Financial Intelligence Unit and the National AML/CFT Committee, Central Bank of Oman AML/CFT Regulatory Guidelines, and MoCIIP Commercial Registry UBO disclosure instructions embedded in the InvestEasy single-window portal.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the UBO or shareholder passport page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's home jurisdiction or competent passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the home-state competent authority — Oman has been a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention since February 2023; for non-HCCH home states, Omani consular legalization is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the local incorporation agent or law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public at the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified Arabic translation authenticated before an Omani notary; consular legalization route applies where the home state is not bound by the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing where the UBO is a corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Omani consular legalization, with certified Arabic translation where required by the MoCIIP registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds and bank reference letter for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank account-holding institution in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or attested by the issuing bank and apostilled where requested for evidence of provenance; Omani notary countersignature for onward filing with the corporate bank or registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory negative screening of the UBO, directors, authorized signatories, and commercial agent against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Omani FIU national watch-list. Any positive PEP hit, including PEP family members and close associates, triggers enhanced due diligence comprising written source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and continuous ownership-event monitoring. Arabic- and English-language open-source negative-news screening is required, and all screening artefacts are retained in the AML/CFT file for the statutory five-year retention period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MoCIIP InvestEasy single-window portal — Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, National Business Center — https://investeasy.om
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal commercial name of an Omani SPC must be rendered in Arabic script. A Latin-script transliteration of the identical Arabic name is registered alongside it and must correspond linguistically; free translation is not permitted. A separate foreign-language trade name may be recorded for SaaS platform branding, but it does not substitute the Arabic legal name. The corporate name must carry the qualifying designation Single Person Company (SPC), in Arabic: شركة الشخص الواحد.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sultani, Royal, Sultanate, Diwan, Palace — reserved for Royal Court and Government entities
Ministry, Government, Public Authority, National — require express ministerial consent
Bank, Insurance, Finance, Investment Fund, Payment, Remittance — trigger CBO or CMA licensing gates notwithstanding the declared ISIC 6201 pure-software scope
Islamic or Sharia — require a recognized regulatory endorsement when used in financial or investment branding
Third-party trademarks and well-known international PropTech marks
Misleading professional or sector tokens inconsistent with the declared ISIC 6201 software activity and NAICS 531390 real-estate ancillary services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection decision, the applicant or its registered agent files a written administrative appeal through the InvestEasy e-request module, or in person at the MoCIIP Central Customer Service Office in Muscat, within 15 working days of the rejection notification. The appeal must cite the Commercial Registration Law, restate the transliteration rationale, and annex the primary ISIC 6201 activity description. MoCIIP must issue a reasoned decision within 5 working days. Concurrent re-filing of an alternative Arabic name without penalty is permitted. One 30-day renewal of an approved name reservation is available if the original voucher remains valid at the time of the renewal request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Hybrid acceptance. The MoCIIP commercial register requires a verifiable Omani street address in the Governorate of Muscat for service of process; a P.O. Box-only virtual address is not accepted for an SPC. Licensed serviced-office and business-center venues are accepted as the registered address. The address must appear on the commercial registration record, match the UBO register entry, and be maintained continuously. The pure software-as-a-service PropTech model qualifies for this lighter physical-substance route, provided a current serviced-office agreement with a licensed Omani business center is in place.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15-20% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of registration, performed by MoCIIP commercial-registration inspectors or Muscat Municipality licence-enforcement officers. Inspection risk is primarily address-verification in nature, and the serviced-office provider must be able to locate the SPC's registered file and a designated person on demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Companies Law of the Sultanate of Oman, Royal Decree No. 18/2019 (Single Person Company provisions, Articles 48-62, and applicable LLC provisions, Articles 249-268); Foreign Capital Investment Law, Royal Decree No. 50/2019; Income Tax Law, Royal Decree No. 28/2009; Value Added Tax Law, Royal Decree No. 121/2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) - Commercial Registry Directorate, Sultanate of Oman; electronic filing through the Invest Easy portal (investeasy.gov.om).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (the 'Incorporation Contract') together with the Commercial Registration application form CR-01 and the name reservation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital under Royal Decree 18/2019. The sole shareholder must declare capital commensurate with the business purpose, fully subscribed at incorporation; no escrow account or bank capital deposit certificate is required for non-regulated IT/software activities, though the Commercial Registrar may request a capital confirmation statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The company is incorporated as a Single Person Company under Oman's Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree 18/2019), with initial share capital fully subscribed by the sole shareholder. (2) The registered office is established at [address], Muscat, Oman, effective immediately. (3) [Name, Passport] is appointed Director and General Manager, authorized to complete incorporation, open bank accounts, retain a statutory auditor, and register with MoCIIP, Oman Tax Authority, OCCI and the Municipality. (4) The opening of a corporate bank account at [Bank] is approved. All prior actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, foreign investor profile, and business scope screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Invest Easy portal (investeasy.gov.om); Investment Services One-Stop-Shop, Muscat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as a foreign investor on the Invest Easy portal using digital identity authentication or a notarized power of attorney. Submit three preferred Arabic/English trade names, select the primary activity 'Computer programming activities (ISIC 6201)' and the supporting scope 'real-estate property management and rental screening cloud services'. The system verifies name uniqueness against the Commercial Register and confirms that the activity falls within the Foreign Capital Investment Law positive list, permitting 100% foreign ownership without ministerial approval.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the sole shareholder
Notarized power of attorney (if acting through a local agent)
Incorporation certificate of the foreign corporate shareholder (if any)
Three proposed company names in Arabic and English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, refile an alternative name immediately. If the activity is screened as restricted, submit a written screening opinion request to the MoCIIP Investment Services Center or narrow the scope to pure software development and SaaS distribution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, review, and notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public, Ministry of Justice, Sultanate of Oman; authenticated electronic copy subsequently registered in Invest Easy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic-language Incorporation Contract containing the corporate name, object clause (ISIC 6201 and ancillary PropTech services), share capital, registered office, manager appointment, and financial year. The notary authenticates the signature of the sole shareholder or the authorized attorney against original identification documents. After notarization, upload the authenticated document in Invest Easy so it becomes part of the Commercial Registration application.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid passports and residential address proof of the shareholder and manager
Name reservation certificate
Evidence of share capital readiness (bank reference or cash flow statement)
Original power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments (e.g., capital adequacy or object clause precision), execute a notarial addendum and re-submit. An unjustified refusal may be challenged before the competent First Instance Court under the Notaries Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Commercial Registration (CR) and issuance of the e-CR certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registry Directorate; Invest Easy portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Incorporation Contract, name reservation, and director consent through the Invest Easy interface. The registrar validates the application and, upon approval, issues the Commercial Registration Number, the electronic CR certificate, and the Commercial Register extract. The e-CR serves as the operating authorization for the software services activity. The Oman Chamber of Commerce registration number is generated simultaneously through automated data exchange. The company must then apply for a Tax Identification Number without delay.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Passport copies and recent photographs of the shareholder and manager
Office lease agreement or address undertaking
Proof of payment of the registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency notice, cure the deficiencies within 30 calendar days in the Invest Easy portal. A rejection may be appealed to the Commercial Registry Directorate Headest admissible under Royal Decree 18/2019, followed by a judicial appeal before the administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Oman Chamber of Commerce membership and municipal business license for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI); Muscat Municipality - Commercial Licenses Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: OCCI membership is activated automatically upon issuance of the Commercial Registration; settle the annual membership fee and obtain the membership certificate. Concurrently file the municipal commercial license application for the office premises, providing the registered lease, floor plan, and zoning information. The municipality assesses building occupancy, signage, and fire safety readiness; the premises are then inspected by the municipality and by the Civil Defense Authority before final approval.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Registered lease agreement or title deed of the office
Floor plan and building occupancy certificate
Civil Defense preliminary clearance or interim no-objection certificate
OCCI membership fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the office site is located in a non-commercial zone, apply for a change-of-use decision from the municipality planning committee. Rejection of the municipal license is appealable to the Governor of Muscat within 15 working days; occupation of the premises is not permitted prior to clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Income tax and VAT registration with the Oman Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA) - Tax Registration Department and e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for corporate income tax within 90 days of incorporation using the CR number, Memorandum, lease, and shareholder details; the Tax Identification Number (TIN) is issued electronically. The entity is subject to the standard 15% corporate income tax rate on Oman-source profits. In parallel, assess VAT registration: registration is mandatory once annual taxable supplies exceed OMR 38,500, and the PropTech SaaS platform should register before invoicing Oman-based clients, applying reverse-charge rules to imported cloud services where applicable.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Office lease agreement
Passport and residency details of the shareholder and manager
Projected revenue statement for VAT threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN is not issued within the stated service level, submit a written escalation to the OTA Customer Service desk with a request for priority processing. Any erroneous VAT effective date may be corrected through the OTA electronic amendment application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening, statutory auditor appointment, and registered governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO) regulated commercial bank in Muscat; MoCIIP Commercial Registry for ongoing corporate filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the sole shareholder as general assembly and adopt the pro-forma resolution. Open the corporate current account with the original CR certificate, authenticated Memorandum, resolution, and KYC documentation. Appoint a licensed auditor as required under the Commercial Companies Law, and file audited financial statements annually with the Oman Tax Authority. Maintain the statutory register of shareholders, minutes, and corporate seal. No economic substance filing is currently required for the active SaaS operating model.
required_dossiers: Approved board resolution of the sole shareholder
Commercial Registration certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
KYC forms and source of funds statement
Engagement letter for the statutory auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a sector regulator confirmation, obtain a letter from MoCIIP confirming that ISIC 6201 SaaS activities are not licensed by a sectoral regulator. A refusal may be escalated through the CBO compliance and consumer protection department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial license is required for pure software/SaaS (ISIC 6201); the applicable authorization bodies for the physical premises are the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) for Commercial Registration, Muscat Municipality for the Business Premises License, and the Public Authority for Civil Defence and Ambulance (PACDA) for fire safety. For any future physical data center, the MoCIIP Industrial Licensing Department would issue an Industrial/Venture License.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Certificate (ISIC 6201 - Computer Programming Activities), Muscat Municipality Commercial/Business Premises License, and PACDA Fire Safety Certificate for the registered office; the Sultanate of Oman does not issue a separate operating permit for SaaS platforms.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Authority of the Sultanate of Oman (EA), Licensing and Environmental Permits Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'Not Triggered / Screening Exempt' for administrative cloud-based SaaS operations. If the registered office hosts physical servers or emergency generators exceeding 10 kVA, the project moves to Category 'B' (Environmental Screening), requiring the EA screening form and a Certificate of Environmental Compliance; a full Category 'A' Environmental Impact Assessment is not applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: General environmental protection obligations under Royal Decree No. 114/2001; workplace noise below 85 dB(A) Leq 8h; electronic waste and toner handling per Ministerial Decree No. 84/2014; no process wastewater or VOC emissions as the business is confined to office operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: PACDA Fire Safety and Means-of-Escape Certificate is mandatory before staff occupancy; Muscat Municipality issues the Building Occupancy and Land Use Clearance after structural inspection under the Oman Unified Building Code (Royal Decree 55/2017). Occupational health obligations under the Labor Law (Royal Decree 35/2003) apply once the first employee is engaged, including first-aid provisioning, fire drills, and workplace safety organization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA), an independent body established under Royal Decree No. 39/2021 and successor to the Secretariat General of Taxation of the Ministry of Finance. Registration portal: OTA e-Services Tax Portal at https://taxy.gov.om (legacy gateway: eservices.tax.gov.om).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Single Person Company (SPC): (1) Incorporate at the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP), obtain Commercial Registration (CR) certificate and authenticated Articles of Association; (2) Appoint an OTA-approved tax agent and file the registration application on the Tax Portal with the CR certificate, capital declaration (no minimum capital statutory requirement), registered office lease, passport copies of the shareholder/directors and POA; (3) OTA verifies and issues a Tax Card containing a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN, 'Al-Raqm Al-Dharibi') that is concurrently used for Corporate Income Tax and VAT; (4) Corporate registration is due within 60 days of commencement of business; VAT registration is due within 30 days from the end of the month in which the mandatory threshold is exceeded or before commencement when registration is compulsory; (5) Registration e-payment and filings thereafter occur through the OTA Tax Portal; foreign entities acting without an Omani place of business must additionally apply for a non-resident VAT ID before selling via local PSPs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SPC (Limited Liability company with one corporate or natural shareholder, RD 18/2019 Commercial Companies Law) is a juridical person and tax resident of Oman; subject to Corporate Income Tax at 15% on worldwide income as adjusted by Omani law (RD 28/2009 as amended by RD 9/2017), with Place of Effective Management (POEM) and incorporation as residency tie-breakers. No pass-through treatment is available to an SPC; Oman-source and PE-attributable income of non-residents are taxed territorially. The PropTech SaaS scope is outside oil/gas, thus no 55% hydrocarbon rate applies. No free-zone incentive is assumed for this entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Oman does NOT operate a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) reduced 3% CIT rate election for qualifying small and medium enterprises with taxable income up to OMR 100,000 (per RD 9/2017 and MOF clarifications); (ii) unilateral foreign tax credit election on a per-country basis for foreign income taxes paid; (iii) VAT grouping election under the VAT Executive Regulations (RD 52/2021) with OTA approval (joint liability regime); (iv) intra-GCC VAT relief/refund election for established foreigners (copy of foreign registration + annual refund form); (v) free-zone tax holiday election (10 years, Duqm 30 years) not exercised here; (vi) no group loss relief except for specified oil and gas joint operations. Oman endorses the OECD BEPS Inclusive Framework, and GCC VAT treaty rules are applied as the primary indirect-tax anti-hybrid overlay.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GCC Value Added Tax (VAT) administered nationally by the OTA under Royal Decree No. 121/2020 (Oman VAT Law) and Executive Regulations RD No. 52/2021, aligned with the Unified VAT Agreement of the GCC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration threshold: OMR 38,500 (approx. USD 100,000) of annual taxable supplies (including zero-rated export supplies; excluding exempt supplies), tested over the preceding 12 months or expected next 12 months. Voluntary registration threshold: OMR 19,250. For a PropTech SaaS exporter selling to non-resident real-estate clients via Stripe/ACH, all zero-ratable export revenue counts toward the threshold, so registration is generally compulsory once billings exceed OMR 38,500 in a rolling year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Oman is implementing a phased National E-Invoicing Framework: the OTA has published technical specifications (structured XML-based e-invoices, machine-readable e-archive, API clearance to the OTA platform) and has piloted the regime with large taxpayers (annual turnover >= OMR 10 million); full mandatory application for all VAT-registered persons, including B2B cross-border SaaS supplies, is being rolled out from 2025-2027 (large-taxpayer phase already effective; SME phase subject to OTA gazettal). Until the mandate fully binds, taxpayers must issue tax invoices in Arabic or English containing all statutory elements, retain electronic records, and support real-time OTA inspection via the Tax Portal. No separate fiscal digital stamp or excise-style stamping applies to software services; API-based clearance will replace download-based e-return submission once the framework becomes mandatory for this SPC.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the international supply of services (export of services), including cloud-based PropTech/SaaS subscription, where: (i) the recipient is a non-resident without an establishment in Oman and is not a citizen/resident for VAT purposes; (ii) the place of supply is governed by the recipient-location rule (B2B) or effective use and enjoyment occurs wholly outside Oman (B2C); (iii) the supplier retains contemporaneous documentary evidence. For SaaS (ISIC 6201/NAICS 531390), B2B sales to remote US/foreign real-estate operators are generally outside the scope of Omani VAT (reported in the export box and zero-rated), while sales to Omani landlords or Omani payment-accepting users are standard-rated at 5%. Express statutory conditions include a written contract, foreign customer VAT-identification or residence certificate, delivery/access evidence from servers outside Oman, and proceeds received in a foreign or licensed Omani bank account in a verifiable manner.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: OTA-compliant zero-rated tax invoice (e-invoice XML/PDF containing OTA TIN, supplier C.R. number, VAT amount '0%', and description of the SaaS subscription delivered to the offshore customer)
Fully executed Software-as-a-Service agreement / order form / property-management platform subscription schedule with non-resident counterparty and invoicing address outside Oman

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit advice from a licensed Omani or foreign bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds within the repatriation window (for ACH/Stripe settlements: consolidated payout and deposit confirmations mapped to each subscription)

Non-resident customer evidence: foreign Commercial Registration, VAT registration certificate, or equivalent tax residence certificate (e.g., W-8BEN-E for US PropTech clients; UK/EU VAT certificate for overseas operators)
Offshore consumption and delivery evidence: SaaS access logs, server location/IP verifications, admin console data attributes proving presence and use outside Oman

Customs Export Declaration (SAD) and transport documents (e.g., Bill of Lading/Airway Bill) - applicability note: required ONLY when the transaction includes physical media or hardware bundled with software; for purely electronic cloud delivery this document is substituted by the digital delivery report above
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Central Bank of Oman exchange-control practice and VAT regulation, proceeds of exported services must be repatriated into an Omani bank account within 180 days; non-repatriation or late collection triggers reassessment of the supply as taxable at 5% plus interest at 15% per annum on any unpaid VAT and fixed penalties (OMR 500-5,000 per erroneous return or invoice; up to OMR 10,000 per registration breach). Fraudulent zero-rating claims (forged contracts, false import/export certificates, circular payments, sham offshore recipients) constitute VAT evasion under RD 121/2020, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fine of OMR 10,000-100,000, extended look-back period of up to 10 years for deliberate concealment, retroactive clawback of credited refunds, and public Blacklist disqualification from future zero-rating or voluntary compliance schemes; OTA special audit desks emphasize invoice-cash-flow-performance congruence for 100% export digital service providers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO), exercising exclusive regulatory authority under the Banking Law (Royal Decree 114/2000), the CBO Exchange Control Rules, and the Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing Law (Royal Decree 30/2016); the CBO supervises inward/outward remittance reporting, foreign-currency account eligibility, and the licensed banking system in the Sultanate of Oman, assisted by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) for corporate licensing and by the Oman Tax Authority for tax-clearance-linked remittance approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Omani Rial (OMR) is fully convertible for current-account purposes under Oman's IMF Article VIII obligations, and capital-account inflows (foreign equity and shareholder loans into an SPC) are freely admitted without prior CBO licensing or exchange-control permission. The SPC may open foreign-currency accounts (USD, EUR, GBP) and repatriate profits in the original currency, subject to the bank's verification of audited financial statements, a valid tax-clearance certificate from the Oman Tax Authority, and the CBO outward-remittance declaration. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal, but a 10% withholding tax applies to dividends, royalties, management fees, and certain service fees paid to non-residents, with treaty rate reductions available under Oman's double-taxation treaty network; no additional capital-gains or repatriation levy applies to a duly capitalized SPC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Oman imposes no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; a SaaS exporter may retain USD, EUR, or GBP balances in a foreign-currency account with a CBO-licensed bank. CBO exchange-control reporting, however, requires that export proceeds be repatriated to the Omani banking system within a commercially reasonable period, with the prevailing bank practice set at 180 days for service exports; the supporting dossier consists of the signed SaaS master agreement, the Stripe/ACH settlement statements, and the periodic foreign-account declaration filed annually with the SPC's relationship bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_market_p: For recurring SaaS revenue collected through offshore payment rails (Stripe Billing and ACH Direct), the CBO-accepted practice is a quarterly sweep of the USD settlement balance from the offshore EMI/US correspondent account into the Omani operational account via SWIFT MT103, so that the bank can complete its balance-of-payments coding and the treasury preserves the OMR/USD peg liquidity profile.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Under-Establishment) plus multi-currency OMR/USD Operational Account
OMR/USD Operational Account with Corporate Internet Banking
USD-denominated Global Banking Account with direct MT103/MT202 clearing
OMR Operational Account with attached USD sub-account
SME Operational Account in OMR and USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year SPC, due by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of OMR 100 to OMR 1,000 plus OMR 10 per day of delay; late payment interest of 1% per month; unfiled returns may be assessed by estimation and the commercial registration renewal may be blocked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) – Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the commercial registration anniversary date; the confirmation must be completed before the expiry of the registered-entity validity in the Commercial Register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under the Commercial Companies Law of up to OMR 500 for late or non-filing; continued default may lead to suspension of the commercial registration and administrative strike-off of the SPC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Oman Tax Authority / MOCIIP Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the financial year-end, accompanying the corporate income tax return; audited statements must also be available for Commercial Registry annual review.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission may result in tax assessment based on estimated income, monetary fines up to OMR 1,000, and suspension of the SPC's commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOCIIP Commercial Registry – Ultimate Beneficial Owner Module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the commercial registration anniversary; any transfer of shares or beneficial-ownership change must be updated in the Commercial Register within 14 calendar days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under the Anti-Money-Laundering Law of up to OMR 10,000 for failure to maintain or update beneficial-owner records; unresolved UBO discrepancies may suspend corporate transactions and registration renewal.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audited financial statements are compulsory for all Omani commercial companies, including a foreign-owned Single Person Company; no SME or low-turnover exemption applies to a registered SPC carrying on a PropTech SaaS business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as applied in Oman; the Commercial Companies Law and Income Tax Law require the annual financial statements to be prepared on a going-concern basis and reconciled to taxable income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SPC must maintain an ultimate beneficial owner register at its registered office and file UBO details with the MOCIIP Commercial Registry. The annual confirmation is due on the commercial registration anniversary. Any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership must be entered in the Register of Members and reported to the Commercial Registry within 14 calendar days; the transfer is effective only after such registration and official record update.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 400 - US$ 1,200 per year for registered agent, commercial address, and administrative liaison services in Muscat.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 1,500 - US$ 3,500 per year for a licensed Omani auditor for a small-scale PropTech SaaS SPC with international payment rails.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS or real-estate property-management SPCs. The Oman Income Tax Law historically grants an OMR 30,000 annual exemption for qualifying small business taxpayers; eligibility depends on ownership, income level, and OTA administrative guidance. The SPC may claim ordinary commercial deductions, capital allowances, and use of tax losses within a five-year carry-forward window.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return — Oman Tax Authority (OTA) e-Portal / Taxoman e-Services; digital form available under the SPC tax file.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months from the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, filing and payment deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Omani Taxpayer Identification Number of the Single Person Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SPC's OTA-issued TPIN; do not use the foreign shareholder's TPIN or TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year ending date and corresponding tax assessment year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 31 December or approved alternative fiscal year-end; attach supporting approval if a non-calendar year is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary business activity code and description of income-producing activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390 for the PropTech real-estate property-management cloud and rental-screening platform. Specify where the servers and management functions are physically performed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross receipts, including SaaS subscription fees, rental management fees, and/or licensing fees before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in OMR using the Oman Central Bank exchange rate for foreign-currency income. All amounts must relate to the Omani taxable presence; apportion revenue attributable to Oman where the SPC has a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimable expenses, including software development, cloud hosting, employee costs, depreciation, marketing, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be actually incurred in Oman or demonstrably attributable to the Omani enterprise. Cross-border management fees and royalties to related parties are restricted unless supported by transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after add-backs and depreciation/capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the OMR 30,000 exemption threshold. For losses, claim carry-forward of no more than five tax years and substantiate the loss schedule from prior OTA assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Tax Reconciliation and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable profit and calculation of the 15% corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Break out any permanent differences, exempt dividend income, non-deductible expenses, and any withholding tax treated as final. Attach calculations for treaty-reduced tax, if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of accuracy signed by an authorised officer or licensed auditor where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The single shareholder or manager must sign electronically. Non-resident individuals must hold an authorised Omani signatory, power of attorney, or e-signature registered with the OTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of OMR 100 to OMR 500 plus OMR 10 per day of continued default. Late payment: 1% monthly surcharge on the unpaid tax. Incorrect or incomplete return: penalty of up to 25% of the additional tax assessed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Oman does not impose statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by an Omani company to any shareholder, including non-resident sole shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Despite the domestic 0% dividend rate, where royalties, interest, or service fees are paid to a treaty-resident beneficial owner, the payer must obtain from the recipient: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, (2) an OTA-approved treaty relief application or exemption declaration, and (3) supporting shareholding/beneficial-ownership documentation. The application is submitted to the Oman Tax Authority before the payment remittance; the OTA will issue a clearance or approve a reduced withholding tax rate at source. A duplicate TRC with Arabic legalisation must be presented if required by procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 10% withholding tax on royalties and 10% withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents. Under many Oman double-taxation agreements, royalty withholding is reduced to 5–10% where the beneficial owner is treaty-resident and satisfies limitation-on-benefits provisions; interest may reduce to 0% or 5% depending on the DTA. The 10% domestic rate applies unless valid DTA relief approval is secured.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: OMR 100,000 — an aggregate annual controlled-transaction threshold for maintaining Local File and Master File in Omani tax practice; statutory law does not publish a fixed Oman threshold, but the OTA will request transfer-pricing documentation for intra-group services, SaaS rights, and software licensing above this risk threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Oman's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under Royal Decree 54/2020 require entities conducting relevant activities — including headquarter, distribution, financing, leasing, and high-risk sectors — to maintain adequate direction, management, physical presence, and employment in Oman. A PropTech SaaS SPC engaged in ISIC 6201 software and real-estate property-management services is not a categorised relevant activity unless it also performs distribution or headquarter functions for a foreign group; nevertheless, the OTA will scrutinise substance to distinguish a genuine trading company from a shell, so physical premises, Omani employees, board decision materiality, and core revenue-generating functions in Oman are required.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting SaaS subscription and rental-screening revenue; issuing false invoices; booking personal expenses of the shareholder as corporate deductions; or hiding income in foreign payment rails (Stripe/ACH settlement accounts) outside the Omani books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Oman's Income Tax Law, tax evasion on conviction carries imprisonment of up to three years and/or a fine not exceeding OMR 50,000, plus the entire evaded tax, a 50% penalty on the under-assessed tax, and monthly late-payment surcharges from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the SPC's corporate veil if the sole shareholder or manager personally directed the evasion; criminal liability extends to the natural person, and civil recovery can reach the shareholder's personal assets, with travel bans and freezing orders available to the OTA during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Omani SPC as a pure pass-through shell: no office, no staff, no board decisions in Oman, all critical SaaS development and rental-screening services performed by the foreign parent, while income is booked in Oman to benefit from the 15% headline rate or treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Designation as an artificial shell results in denial of tax residence, reassessment of Oman-source income, a penalty equivalent to 10% of revenue or OMR 10,000 under ESR non-compliance powers, cancellation of the commercial licence, and loss of Omani tax treaty protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The single shareholder and authorised manager are jointly and severely liable for the shell's tax deficiencies if assets are intermingled; the OTA can issue a personal assessment, freeze personal bank accounts, and impose a five-year ban on serving as a director in Oman.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging artificially low prices to the foreign SaaS platform parent for software licences, or paying inflated royalty/cloud-service fees to the parent without an arm's-length benchmark, resulting in Oman taxable profits being stripped out.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The OTA has authority to adjust income using the arm's-length standard; the adjustment attracts a 25% penalty on the additional tax, a daily late-payment surcharge, and, in case of non-disclosure of related-party transactions, an additional administrative fine of up to OMR 20,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who knowingly approved unsubstantiated intercompany prices are personally liable for the tax adjustment where they benefit directly from the shifted funds; the OTA may restrain their travel and impose a criminal penalty if the documentation is false.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Profit Repatriation / Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring outbound payments as tax-free 'dividends' on preference shares while the substance is loan interest or a royalty; alternatively, remitting dividends to a non-resident and falsely certifying zero withholding tax to avoid the 10% royalty/interest withholding on cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under substance-over-form principles triggers the 10% withholding tax plus a penalty of 25% of the unpaid withholding; continuing non-compliance leads to daily surcharge and denial of deductions for the unpaid payment, increasing corporate income tax at 15%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs a false withholding declaration commits tax perjury and is personally liable for withholding remittances; a criminal conviction can impose imprisonment up to two years and prohibition from acting as an officer of any Omani company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Running a PropTech rental-screening payment platform through Stripe Billing and ACH direct rails without applying customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership checks, or sanctions screening, and thereby facilitating transfers tied to an unlicensed money service or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Oman's Anti-Money Laundering Law (Royal Decree 30/2016) exposes the SPC to fines up to OMR 50,000 per breach, suspension or revocation of electronic-payment authorisation, freeze of settlement accounts, and administrative fines by the National Centre for Financial Information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be held personally criminally liable if they knew or recklessly ignored the laundering risk; penalties include imprisonment of up to seven years, confiscation of assets, and a permanent ban from financial-sector management.
